about: I am a Ph.D. student in Environmental Engineering at the University of Southern California, advised by Jiachen Zhang. I received my bachelor’s degrees in Engineering and Economics from Tsinghua University.

My research examines the interactions among climate, the built environment, and energy infrastructure. I study how urban form and anthropogenic heat shape local climate, how climate change affects energy and water use, and how we can design more resilient energy systems.

A particular focus of my work is data centers: their local climate impacts, cooling resources and technologies, infrastructure siting, and opportunities for waste-heat recovery. My work draws on atmospheric modeling, energy-system analysis, economics, and machine learning, informed by experience in the nuclear energy industry.

news.text: Received the CESASC Jonathan H. Jiang (JHJ) Physics Prize.
Our study of urban morphology, meteorology, and heat stress in Southern California was published in JGR: Atmospheres.
Our study of anthropogenic heat in Los Angeles was published in JGR: Atmospheres (co-first author).
Our study of emissions from the 2025 Los Angeles fires was accepted by ACS ES&T Air.
Received the USC Viterbi Das Family Travel Award and an A&WMA Student Scholarship.
